A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. The main text, three figures, equations and Appendices A–E support a reliable comparison despite reflow and shortened proofs.

before.justification: Section 2.4 and Figure 2(b) report original simulations of population-gradient-descent training with d = 2048, P = 1024, Hermite-4 activation and varying student widths.

after.justification: V2 retains the original population-gradient-descent simulations and empirical loss curves in Section 2.4 and Figure 2(b).

M1.justification: The two-layer, 2-homogeneous student model, MSE objective, initialization and online SGD update are retained. Changes to greedy selection concern the analytical ordering of neurons.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic Gaussian teacher–student task with Hermite-4 activation and power-law teacher weights. No additional dataset, domain or evaluation scenario appears in the appendices.

E2.justification: Figure 2 retains the same idealized scaling comparison and empirical student-width curves. No evaluated comparison algorithm is added or removed; the new citations are theoretical references.

E3.justification: Section 2.4 retains d = 2048, P = 1024, beta = 0.8, Hermite-4 activation, fixed-step-size population GD and varying student widths. The MSE-versus-compute evaluation is unchanged.

E4.justification: The width-dependent scaling illustration and comparison of idealized and empirical curves are retained. Neither version contains additional empirical ablations, robustness tests or case studies.

E5.justification: Figure 2's shaded curves and their reporting are unchanged. Neither version specifies simulation seeds, repeated-run counts or statistical tests. The revised analytical tail bound belongs to T1.

E6.justification: The Figure 2 plot images are identical, including the labeled theoretical slope of -0.33 and empirical slope of -0.38. The reported staircase, power-law decay and approximation-plateau findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Assumption 2.1(b) replaces the Lipschitz-or-polynomial restriction with polynomial growth of both sigma and its derivative. Lemma B.1 changes its tail parameter from 2 or 1+2Q to 4(1+Q), replacing the explicit variance/tail proof and old Lemma B.2 with references and an independence qualification. Greedy-selection overlap powers change from 2 to 2I-2, matching the existing general-I analysis. These are localized revisions; the main recovery and scaling-law statements are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same central claims: polynomial-complexity single-phase learning, sharp neuron-recovery transitions and loss scaling with training steps/samples and student width.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 explicitly qualifies the role of small initialization: small neuron norms alone do not prevent attraction to stronger teacher directions. V2 emphasizes incoherence preserved through sharp transitions as the mechanism enabling decoupling. The conclusion's limitations and proposed extensions are unchanged.

D1.justification: The algorithm, initialization and simulation-setting disclosures are retained. V2 adds no implementation instructions, hardware information, training-time measurements or code/data access information.

R1.justification: V2 adds GWB25 and KC22, removes AW15 and VH16, and attributes the gradient variance/tail argument to the already-cited RL24. The broader research positioning and Appendix A remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 3.2 is locally rewritten and shortened, Appendix B.1's exposition is condensed, and the B.2 heading and equation cross-references are revised. The overall section organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is reduced in size and its matrix-entry labels use powers 2I-2; its caption and surrounding text reflow. Several equations receive more compact formatting. Figures 1 and 2 are retained, with no figures or tables added or removed.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves consistency by aligning greedy-selection weights with Lemma 3.1 and clarifies the decoupling mechanism in Section 3.2. The revised growth assumption and tail bound refine the theoretical scope. A tradeoff is that Appendix B.1 becomes less self-contained when detailed proofs are replaced by citations. The main guarantees and simulations remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
